check.reason: The target is the insurers and market consolidation, so it punches at the system. Patients are treated as people with limited choices, and the joke is on the insurers. It accurately reflects the story (the AMA warning about a few payers controlling markets) without invented numbers, quotes or results. It does not mock the reporter or the AMA, and it names no private individual. It avoids death, children and violence. The tone is dry and deadpan, and the irony of 'competition' among a handful of firms is genuinely satirical.

pick.title: Just a handful of payers control US health insurance markets, AMA warns
pick.headline: Handful of Insurers Celebrate Fiercely Competitive Market of Handful of Insurers
pick.take: The AMA warns that a few payers control US insurance markets. Fortunately, competition survives: the same few companies still vie to set the premiums, narrow the networks, and design the prior authorization forms. Patients are free to choose, provided they enjoy the menu. Physicians, meanwhile, negotiate from a position best described as supplicant.
